subject: saw-scaled viper
title: The Snake That Kills the Most People Is Shorter Than Your Arm

scenes.text: The deadliest snake on Earth is shorter than your arm.
It isn't a cobra. It isn't a mamba. It's the saw-scaled viper: one to three feet long, hiding in dry scrub from Africa through Arabia to India and Sri Lanka.
It's believed to kill more people than every other snake species put together. Not because its venom is the strongest.
Because of where it lives: dry farmland and footpaths where people walk, and it bites when it's stepped on. Mortality after a bite is high.
Its warning is a sound: it rubs its rough, saw-edged scales together and makes a hissing, sawing rasp.
Thirty inches of snake. More deaths than every cobra, mamba and taipan combined.

description:
The deadliest snake on Earth is not a cobra or a mamba, it is the saw-scaled viper, a snake just one to three feet long.
Saw-scaled vipers (genus Echis) live in arid regions and dry savannas north of the Equator across Africa, Arabia and southwestern Asia to India and Sri Lanka. They are believed to be responsible for more human deaths than all other snake species combined, and mortality after a bite is high. Before striking, they rub their oblique, serrated scales together to produce a rasping, hissing warning.
Would you have guessed the deadliest snake is this small?
first_comment: Smaller than most garden snakes, yet it out-kills cobras and mambas. Which snake did you think was the deadliest?
